inputs.name: settled values
inputs.cite: records M-606, M-005, M-006 (cited, not recomputed)

day.reading: X/Y exists for any count and duration; a mean needs no Gaussian; 4N_e is itself an average
day.holds: existence and the Gaussian point hold as arithmetic; both sides accept existence (G1b UJ-02, G1c CA-10). Day concedes rates need their parameters (evo007@L31)

critic.reading: the average is uninformative without the distribution and the conditions
critic.holds: the mean need not be a typical event (bimodal test: mean 35,625, no member near it; 4N_e has CV 0.538, M-606), and an average from one system bounds another only under a transfer model (M-005, M-006). 'Meaningless' read literally (does not exist) fails; read as 'not a bound or a typical time' it holds

notes: Inference object; no number is printed in the rows. Existence is arithmetic and not in dispute. The relayed critic sentences say 'meaningless', not 'does not exist'; under the reading 'not informative as a bound or a typical time' they are correct, and that reading is the one Day answers with 'rates require specifying the relevant parameters'. Whether an observed average bounds a rate elsewhere is the transfer question of M-006 and M-103, not this object. The bimodal sample is a constructed test point.
